title: The Promise That Outlived Its Convenience
script: Citra: [thoughtful] Hanif, do you remember promising, years ago, that you'd be the one to walk my father to his seat if I ever got married?
Hanif: Of course I remember. Why do you ask like you expect me to have forgotten something that specific?
Citra: [carefully] Because the wedding is now the same weekend as the conference you've been preparing for since January, and I'd understand if something had to give.
Hanif: Nothing has to give. A promise made casually years ago doesn't become optional just because keeping it turned out to be inconvenient.
Citra: [reflective] That's generous of you to say, but conferences like this don't come around twice, and I don't want you resenting a decision made out of obligation.
Hanif: I don't think obligation and resentment are automatically the same thing, though people often talk as if they were.
Citra: [honestly] What's the difference, in your mind?
Hanif: Resentment is what happens when you keep a promise while secretly wishing you hadn't made it. I don't wish that, not for a second.
Citra: [gently] I suppose I've been quietly testing whether you'd release yourself from it, the way most people would given a good enough excuse.
Hanif: I noticed that, actually, and decided not to give you the satisfaction of an easy answer.
Citra: [calmly] Fair enough. So the conference gets rescheduled?
Hanif: The conference gets rescheduled. It's a professional inconvenience, not a moral one, and those two things deserve very different weights.
Citra: [encouraging] I don't think I've ever heard anyone describe a scheduling conflict in quite such serious terms.
Hanif: Promises are only serious in the moments they're inconvenient to keep. Otherwise they're just plans, and plans don't require character.
Citra: [seriously] Then thank you, properly this time, for a promise I half expected circumstances to quietly erase.
Hanif: Circumstances don't get a vote on this one. I'll be there, conference or no conference.

quiz.question: What promise had Hanif made to Citra years earlier?
options: To walk her father to his seat if she ever got married
To give a speech at her wedding
To pay for her wedding
To be her business partner
quiz.explanation: Hanif had promised years ago to be the one to walk Citra's father to his seat at her wedding.

quiz.question: Why does Citra think Hanif might need to break the promise?
options: The wedding falls on the same weekend as a conference he has prepared for since January
He no longer wants to attend
He is moving abroad
He disapproves of the marriage
quiz.explanation: The wedding is the same weekend as a conference Hanif has been preparing for since January.

quiz.question: How does Hanif distinguish obligation from resentment?
options: He says they are always the same thing
Obligation only applies to strangers
Resentment is a sign of true commitment
Resentment is keeping a promise while secretly wishing you hadn't made it, which he does not feel
quiz.explanation: Hanif explains that resentment is keeping a promise while secretly wishing you hadn't made it, and he insists he doesn't feel that.

quiz.question: What does Citra admit she had been doing throughout the conversation?
options: Planning to cancel the wedding
Trying to convince Hanif to skip the wedding
Quietly testing whether Hanif would release himself from the promise given a good excuse
Hiding the conference conflict from him
quiz.explanation: Citra admits she had been quietly testing whether Hanif would release himself from the promise the way most people would.

quiz.question: How does Hanif ultimately distinguish a promise from a plan?
options: There is no real difference between them
Plans are more important than promises
Promises are only serious in the moments they're inconvenient to keep, while plans don't require character
Promises can always be rescheduled without consequence
quiz.explanation: Hanif says promises are only serious in the moments they're inconvenient to keep; otherwise they're just plans, which don't require character.

quiz.question: Why does Hanif refuse to treat the conference as a release from his promise?
options: Reputation protection causes the narrator to damage an innocent colleague.
Later inconvenience cannot convert a commitment into an optional plan.
He called passive tolerance patience while deadlines repeatedly failed.
Higher-cost purchases require independent review before commitment.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: Later inconvenience cannot convert a commitment into an optional plan.

quiz.question: What distinction does Hanif draw between obligation and resentment?
options: Performed modesty had coexisted with fragile confidence and inflated competence.
Keeping a promise unwillingly differs from valuing the promise despite cost.
It tolerates difficulty while deliberately moving toward resolution.
The mistake remains recorded while deliberate falsification is prevented.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: Keeping a promise unwillingly differs from valuing the promise despite cost.

quiz.question: Why does Citra admit she has been testing him?
options: It is an accurate public account of one's limitations.
It tests whether waiting benefits improvement or merely postpones discomfort.
Accurate disclosure reveals a process weakness that also needs correction.
She expects sufficient inconvenience to make most promises disappear.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: She expects sufficient inconvenience to make most promises disappear.

quiz.question: How does describing the conflict as professional rather than moral guide the decision?
options: Career inconvenience carries less weight than freely given commitment.
It shows that competence can survive honest admission of error.
Their anxiety and confrontation contrast with passivity's quiet appearance.
It consists of accepting embarrassment when truthful records require it.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: Career inconvenience carries less weight than freely given commitment.

quiz.question: What claim about character explains why inconvenient promises matter most?
options: Protecting reputation and protecting truth often demand different responses.
Commitment becomes morally meaningful when circumstances make it costly.
The behaviour is probably avoidance rather than patience.
The account remains no less truthful than the event it records.
quiz.explanation: This interpretation follows the speaker's reasoning: Commitment becomes morally meaningful when circumstances make it costly.
